topic.subject: science
topic.title: Our environment
topic.scope: ecosystem, food chains and webs, trophic levels, 10 percent law, biological magnification, ozone layer, waste management

misconceptions.statement: An ecosystem consists only of living organisms like plants and animals.
misconceptions.why: Students often focus on the biological components and ignore the physical environment.
misconceptions.fix: An ecosystem includes both biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components like sunlight, water, and soil interacting together.

probe.question: Is a pond with water, rocks, and sunlight but no fish still an ecosystem?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because there are no living things in it.

misconceptions.statement: Energy is created as it moves up the food chain.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the increase in complexity of organisms with an increase in energy content.
misconceptions.fix: Energy is lost at each trophic level as heat during respiration and metabolic activities, so it decreases as you move up.

probe.question: Which trophic level has the most energy available?
probe.wrong_answer: The top carnivore because it is the biggest and strongest.

concepts.name: Energy Transfer and the 10 Percent Law

misconceptions.statement: The 90 percent of energy lost is destroyed or disappears.
misconceptions.why: Students interpret 'loss' as total disappearance rather than transformation into a different form.
misconceptions.fix: The energy is not destroyed; it is converted into heat energy and released into the environment during life processes.

probe.question: What happens to the 90% of energy not passed to the next level?
probe.wrong_answer: It is completely destroyed and no longer exists in the universe.

misconceptions.statement: Chemicals like pesticides become more concentrated because organisms at the top eat more food.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the volume of food consumed rather than the inability of the body to excrete non-biodegradable substances.
misconceptions.fix: Magnification happens because non-biodegradable chemicals accumulate in the tissues of organisms and are passed on to the next level, increasing in concentration.

probe.question: Why do eagles have higher levels of DDT than the fish they eat?
probe.wrong_answer: Because eagles eat a very large quantity of fish every day.

misconceptions.statement: The ozone hole is caused by global warming and the greenhouse effect.
misconceptions.why: Students conflate two major environmental issues they hear about in the news.
misconceptions.fix: The ozone layer is depleted primarily by CFCs, while global warming is caused by greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide.

probe.question: Does reducing carbon dioxide emissions directly fix the ozone hole?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because carbon dioxide is the main gas that destroys the ozone layer.
